patch_description:
This implementation replaces the prefix beam search with an adaptive large-neighborhood search (ALNS) approach:

1. It builds several diverse objective-guided schedules using randomized greedy construction.
2. It scores every tested partial or complete ordering using `workload.get_opt_seq_cost`, rather than relying on transaction size or write counts.
3. It repeatedly destroys portions of elite schedules by removing transactions from random, contiguous, and high-disruption regions.
4. It repairs each destroyed schedule by greedily selecting the transaction-position insertion with the lowest exact simulator cost.
5. It applies targeted relocation and swap improvements to completed schedules.
6. It preserves an elite pool of different good schedules, allowing the search to escape local minima instead of optimizing only one greedy schedule.

Destroy-and-repair changes multiple transaction relationships simultaneously, which can discover schedules unavailable to simple swaps, insertions, or beam-prefix decisions.
